question.leadin: One noblewoman from this family was blamed for instigating a massacre of thousands of Huguenots in France on St. Bartholomew's Day.
question.text: Name this European family to which Catherine, the wife of King Henry II, belonged. Cosimo established this family's dominance over the city of Florence during the Renaissance.
question.answerHtml: Medici [MEH-dih-chee] family (accept Catherine de’ Medici or Cosimo de’ Medici )
question.clue: People with this last name founded a Platonic Academy and were targeted in the Pazzi Conspiracy.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the newspaper Avanti!
swap.text: Although he had formerly edited it, this fascist leader banned the publication of Avanti! when he took power. Nicknamed "Il Duce", he led the Blackshirts during the March on Rome.
swap.clue: Futurist artists glorified this leader, who began the Pacification of Libya.

question.text: While in office, LaGuardia worked with Thomas Dewey to prosecute such gangsters as Lucky Luciano, who belonged to this criminal organization based in Italy.
question.answerHtml: the Sicilian mafia [or Cosa Nostra; or the Five Families; prompt on “the mob ”]
question.clue: Giovanni Falcone was killed by this organization for prosecuting its members, who follow the omerta code.

swap.leadin: Many Carbonari, or "charcoal burners," participated in this movement.
swap.text: Name this nineteenth-century movement that called for the formation of a modern-day country. After this movement succeeded, Victor Emmanuel II became the first king of that country.
swap.clue: The Siege of Gaeta ended the "Expedition of the Thousand" for this cause in which the Redshirts helped conquer the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

question.leadin: Answer the following about things named Barbarossa.
question.text: Andrea Doria, an admiral from this maritime rival city of Venice, led the Holy League when it was defeated by Hayreddin Barbarossa at the Battle of Preveza.
question.answerHtml: Genoa [or Genova; or Genua; or the Republic of Genoa; or Reppublica di Genova; or Repubrica de Zena]
question.clue: This city was led for much of its history by the Boccanegra family and was the home of admiral Andrea Doria.

swap.leadin: The traditional end of this military expedition is said to be the meeting of its leader with a king at Teano.
swap.text: Name this campaign, where Giuseppe Garibaldi's Red Shirts conquered Calabria. Its success led to the annexation of the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies into the Kingdom of Sardinia.
swap.clue: The primary opponent was Francis II, who was decisively defeated at Milazzo after failing to stop a landing at Marsala.

question.text: This author of "The Prince" wrote a series of discourses on the Roman historian Livy, the author of works such as Ab Urbe Condita.
question.clue: After the republic he worked for was overthrown, this historian was placed under house arrest and wrote a treatise dedicated to his new ruler.

swap.text: Francis I was locked in the Pizzighettone ("Peet-see-get-TOH-nay") and forced to sign the Treaty of Madrid after being captured by Charles V at this 1525 battle during the Italian Wars.
swap.clue: Alfonso d'Avalos, the Marquis of Pescara, led the arquebusiers under the overall command of Charles de Lannoy; he breached the wall of Mirabello around midnight and many combatants drowned in the nearby Ticino River.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Romulus Augustulus, the final emperor of the Western Roman Empire.
question.text: From 402 until the collapse of the Roman Empire, this city served as its capital. In later times, this city was the seat of the Kingdom of Lombardy.
question.clue: It became the seat of the Byzantine governor of Italy in the sixth century, and its namesake Cosmography was written around 700.

swap.text: Brazil's memorial honors members of the Brazilian Expeditionary Force killed trying to capture this Axis defensive position. Operation Olive partially broke through this line defended by Albert Kesselring in Italy's Apennine ("APP-uh-nine") Mountains.
swap.clue: The U.S. 10th Mountain Division was deployed at Riva Ridge at the Battle of Monte Castello in the winter of 1944, during General Clark's assault on this northernmost defensive fortification in Italy.

question.text: This Italian fashion designer was shot by Cunanan while returning from a shopping trip outside his Miami Beach home.

swap.text: Among Cavour's tasks was controlling Francesco Crispi and this man, a former Carbonari, and the military leader of the Italian unification.
swap.clue: This leader of the Red Shirts who overthrew the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

question.leadin: Answer these things about assassinations in Italian history.
question.text: This king imposed martial law and awarded Fiorenzo Bava-Beccaris a medal for his brutal repression of riots in Milan. These actions later led to his assassination by Gaetano Bresci.
question.clue: This ruler's lost popularity for supporting the Bava-Beccaris massacre in Milan.

swap.leadin: This 1848 insurrection successfully drove Austrian soldiers out of its city after nearly a week of street fighting.
swap.text: Name this insurrection against Marshal Radetzik which began the First Italian War of Independence.
swap.clue: This event during which children in hats and tailed jackets from the Martinitt orphanage spread information. Cattaneo and Casati led street-fighting insurgents during this event.

question.text: Thousands of Mussolini's Blackshirts tried to force the hand of the Luigi Facta government with this October 1922 demonstration. Mussolini himself did not actually participate, remaining in Milan in case this demonstration failed.
question.clue: Mussolini came to power in this 1922 event, in which the Blackshirt paramilitaries of the Fascist Party threatened insurrection until Victor Emmanuel III convinced Prime Minister Luigi Facta to resign.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about leagues in European history.
swap.text: This 1508 league was organized by Julius II against Venice, but the pope flip-flopped and allied with Venice later, proclaiming a "Holy League" against France.
swap.clue: Its opponent blamed the defeat on the indecisive leadership of Leonardo Loredan, which was thought to have contributed to the loss at Agnadello.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Italian politics during the First World War.
question.text: This man headed the Italian delegation to the Paris Peace Conference to round out the "Big Four." He served as prime minister of Italy from 1917 to 1919.
question.clue: This leader who upset nationalists by failing to address the broken London Pact.

swap.text: After the Bajamonte Tiepolo against the Doge in 1310, this secretive council was created, named for the original number of its members, and given emergency powers in Venice. It was led by men called Capi who were confined to live in the Doge's Palace.
swap.clue: Prior to becoming doge, Faliero served in this body that secretly monitored the activities of all Venetians. Citizens could submit information to this body by placing letters in bocche di leone ("BOKE-kay dee lay-OH-nay").

question.leadin: The Cooper Union speech tars John Brown by association with this man, whose actions prompted Palmerston to introduce a Conspiracy to Murder Bill that brought down his government.
question.text: Name this Italian nationalist who used mercury fulminate to craft his namesake bombs, which gained popularity with 19th-century terrorists after he lobbed them at Napoleon III in an 1858 assassination attempt.
question.clue: Mazzini sent this man to begin an uprising in Carrara. Lord Palmerston's first government collapsed after this man's failed assassination attempt on Napoleon III.

swap.text: Texts from Monte Cassino used this Latin script that resembled Roman cursive with its fluid, closely-spaced letters. Writing in this Southern Italian script declined relative to late Caroline and Gothic scripts after the Norman conquests.
swap.answerHtml: Beneventan script [or scrittura beneventana; or word forms like script of Benevento; accept Lombardic script, Langobardic script, scrittura langobarda, scrittura longobardisca, or word forms]
